facts.statement: Platypterygius is a genus of Cretaceous ichthyosaurs with the name meaning "flat fin".
facts.quote: Platypterygius (meaning "flat fin") is a historically paraphyletic genus of platypterygiine ichthyosaur from the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Species assigned to Platypterygius were generally large-bodied macropredators characterized by robust teeth.
facts.quote: Generally, species referred to this genus were large bodied macropredators based on their robust dentition.

facts.statement: Platypterygius reached a length of approximately 7 meters.
facts.quote: Platypterygius alcanzaba una longitud de aproximadamente 7 metros.

facts.statement: The animal possessed a long snout and a powerful tail equipped with fins.
facts.quote: Tenía un hocico largo y cola poderosa provista de aletas.

facts.statement: Platypterygius had more digits in its forefins than is usual for ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Tenía más dígitos en las aletas anteriores de lo usual para los ictiosaurios.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from P. australis includes hatchling protostegid sea turtles and enantiornithine birds found alongside fish in its gut contents.
facts.quote: This is also supported by P. australis having been found with remains of hatchling protostegid sea turtles and enantiornithines (possibly Nanantius) in association with actinopterygian fish in its guts.

facts.statement: Like other ichthyosaurs, Platypterygius was viviparous.
facts.quote: Como los demás ictiosaurios, Platypterygius era vivíparo.

facts.statement: A specimen of P. australis from Australia preserved gut contents of cephalopods, fish, and pterosaurs, as well as bite marks likely made by Kronosaurus queenslandicus.
facts.quote: White et al. (2026) describe a dismembered specimen of Platypterygius australis from the Lower Cretaceous (Albian) Toolebuc Formation (Australia), preserved with gut contents including cephalopod, fish and pterosaur remains, and preserving evidence of bite marks likely produced by Kronosaurus queenslandicus

facts.statement: The interpretation that a specific P. australis specimen preserved gut contents is contested by some researchers.
facts.quote: their interpretation of the studied specimen as preserved with gut contents is contested by Poropat & Nielsen-Smith (2026)

facts.statement: While fossils of Platypterygius have been found on different continents, the holotype specimen was discovered in Germany.
facts.quote: While fossils referred to Platypterygius have been found throughout different continents, the holotype specimen was found in Germany.

facts.statement: Platypterygius lived during the Late Aptian to Late Cenomanian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Aptian-Late Cenomanian

facts.statement: Platypterygius lived in the Early Cretaceous in what is now Australia, Russia, the United States, Germany, and possibly New Zealand.
facts.quote: que vivieron en el Cretácico Inferior en lo que hoy es Australia, Rusia, Estados Unidos, Alemania y posiblemente Nueva Zelanda.

facts.statement: The time range for Platypterygius is estimated from 161.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Cenomanian (161.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Platypterygius was historically used as a wastebasket taxon, with many species likely being undiagnostic or representing distinct genera.
facts.quote: It was historically used as a wastebasket taxon, and most species within Platypterygius likely are undiagnostic at the genus or species level, or represent distinct genera, even being argued as invalid.

facts.statement: Research in the 2000s and 2010s showed that the defining features of Platypterygius were either not present in all assigned species or were also found in other ophthalmosaurids.
facts.quote: Later research conducted in the 2000s and 2010s has repeatedly shown this to be false, with all of the autapomorphies previously used to define Platypterygius either not being present in all assigned species or also being present in other ophthalmosaurids.

facts.statement: An analysis by Zverkov and Jacobs (2020) showed that P. americanus is too distantly related to other species within the genus.
facts.quote: The following cladogram shows the internal relationships of ophthalmosaurian ichthyosaurs according to an analysis performed by Zverkov and Jacobs (2020) which shows that P. americanus is too distantly related compared to the other three species.

facts.statement: Platypterygius is the genus most closely related to Caypullisaurus and Brachypterygius.
facts.quote: Es el género más relacionado con Caypullisaurus y Brachypterygius

facts.statement: The type species was described in 1922 based on remains from Germany that had previously been described as Ichthyosaurus platydactylus in 1907 by Ferdinand Broili.
facts.quote: The type species of Platypterygius was described in 1922 based on remains found in upper Aptian strata around Hannover, Germany that were previously described as a species of Ichthyosaurus (I. platydactylus) in 1907 by Ferdinand Broili.

facts.statement: The original remains used to describe the type species were not adequately described and were destroyed during World War 2.
facts.quote: These remains however were not adequately described and to complicate matters further, destroyed during World War 2.

facts.statement: In 1998, Arkhangelsky estimated that P. platydactylus was about 5 meters long and P. americanus was about 5.5 meters long.
facts.quote: In 1998, Arkhangelsky estimated that P. platydactylus was about 5 m long, while "P." americanus was about 5.5 m long.

facts.statement: In 2010, Zammit and colleagues estimated that P. australis was about 7 meters long.
facts.quote: In 2010, Zammit and colleagues estimated that "P." australis was about 7 m long.

facts.statement: Several species of Platypterygius include described specimens of juveniles, newborns, and pregnant females.
facts.quote: Se han descrito varias especies, entre las cuales se encuentran especímenes juveniles, recién nacidos y hembras preñadas.
